status: Proposed revision only; no human approval or publication
source_context: 16 report entries, 15 distinct URLs; issuer guidelines/platform documentation, not 16 independent studies. 13 sources cited publicly. Source bodies were read by research agents; this synthesis read their full reports and structured ledgers, not an independent re-fetch.

sources.title: A Taxonomy of Evaluation
sources.author: Professor Jim Macnamara for AMEC
sources.read_scope: Complete extracted page, including taxonomy, footnotes and references.
principles: Do not substitute lower-level metrics for higher-level outcomes.
Outputs concern distribution/exposure/reception; outtakes attention/understanding/engagement; outcomes audience effects; impact organizational/stakeholder/societal results.
Stages overlap and feedback is iterative, not a simple linear funnel.
Impact may take years; causation requires temporal order, a supported relationship and ruling out other causes as far as possible.
limits: Communications evaluation taxonomy, not an empirical validation of a Riggg session scorecard.
Metric classifications depend on purpose; outtakes overlap short-term outcomes.
sources.applicability: Separate shipped assets, audience reception, meaningful response and business effects in one recorded-session review.

sources.title: AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework — Home
sources.author: Richard Bagnall; AMEC working group introduction
sources.read_scope: Complete extracted page; linked resources/webinar not treated as read.
principles: Align communication objectives to organizational objectives before activity.
Establish benchmarks, targets and KPIs in advance, then revisit results.
Measurement should move beyond activity counts toward meaningful effects.
locators: Introduction to the new interactive tool
limits: Planning guidance, not universal KPI values, a causal study or an episode timing prescription.
sources.applicability: Pre-recording objective/measurement brief and later review; retain Riggg ownership of the 5Ps.

sources.title: Podcast Measurement Technical Guidelines, Version 2.2
sources.author: IAB Tech Lab Podcast Technical Working Group, in partnership with IAB Audio Committee; lead Katie Stroud
sources.read_scope: All 29 PDF pages read via pypdf in three chunks. Cover typography partly garbled and text spaces often absent; substantive sections legible.
principles: Server-side download delivery is not confirmed playback.
Valid downloads require filtering, file thresholds and deduplication; one-minute content threshold is downloaded bytes, not one minute heard.
Declare fixed versus rolling 24-hour measurement windows and methodology.
Listeners inferred from IP/user-agent combinations require a stated time frame and have over/undercount risks.
Summing episode downloads does not give unique audience.
Only certified organizations can claim compliance.
limits: Technical downloaded-podcast/ad-measurement guidance, not proof of attention, business impact, or Riggg/provider certification.
Do not transfer its one-minute download rule to video engagement or its 24-hour dedupe rule to a 30-day business review.
sources.applicability: Record host metric definition, provider/methodology and reporting window; keep downloads apart from platform listening.

sources.title: Check your YouTube thumbnail impressions and watch time
sources.author: YouTube Help
sources.read_scope: Complete HTML response fetched (1,617,429 bytes); full article text read after initial web_fetch body cap.
principles: Registered impressions require more than one second with at least 50% thumbnail visibility.
External embeds, emails and several other surfaces are excluded from thumbnail impressions.
Views from impressions are a subset of views; watch time is a separate measure.
Cards and funnel reports may update at different times.
locators: Impressions and how they led to watch time
limits: YouTube-specific evolving definitions and scoped denominator; not all exposure or verified target-audience reach.
sources.applicability: Use native registered-impression CTR rather than all views divided by impressions; separate exposure, viewing and action.

sources.title: Measure key moments for audience retention
sources.author: YouTube Help
sources.read_scope: Complete HTML response fetched (1,625,222 bytes); full article text read including graph guidance and segment definitions.
principles: Retention generally takes 1–2 days to process and is video-level.
Compare similar-length videos; inspect intro, top moments, spikes and dips.
A spike can signal either interest/rewatching or confusion; a dip can be skipping or abandonment.
Highlighted moments require detection and a video at least 60 seconds long with at least 100 views.
Segment organic/paid and new/returning audiences where available.
locators: View audience retention by segment type
limits: Platform diagnostic observations, not causal proof of why viewers leave or a universal retention benchmark.
Highlight eligibility is not a statistical significance threshold.
sources.applicability: Attach timestamps to an editorial improvement hypothesis; do not convert a graph spike into demonstrated understanding.

sources.title: Analytics
sources.author: Apple Podcasts for Creators
sources.read_scope: Complete extracted page including episode metrics and performance comparisons.
principles: Apple reports aggregated listening/viewing completion based on unique devices, distinct from host downloads.
Engaged listeners heard/watched at least 20 minutes or 40% of an episode.
Average consumption is average percentage per device and can exceed 100% with repeat listening.
Performance compares equal days since release (7, 14, 30 or 60) with median/average/top baselines.
At least five unique listeners must play show content for selected-period data to appear.
limits: Apple audience only; not all podcast listeners.
Five-listener threshold is data availability, not representative-sample adequacy.
Show followers are not automatically attributable to one episode.
sources.applicability: Use episode listeners and consumption, label engaged-listener denominator, compare equal release ages, mark unavailable data rather than zero.

sources.title: Get started with attribution
sources.author: Google Analytics Help
sources.read_scope: Complete HTML response fetched (1,680,811 bytes); full article text including advanced methodology read.
principles: Attribution assigns credit under a rule or model to touchpoints.
Models differ; reporting model, eligible channels and lookback window are settings.
Data-driven methodology uses converting/nonconverting paths and modeled counterfactuals; conversions can be reattributed for up to seven days.
limits: Google advertising/analytics system documentation; its modeled methodology does not establish incremental causal ROI for a single organic recorded session.
Tracked paths and assigned credit are not a complete history of influence.
sources.applicability: Record model/window and distinguish observed referral, self-report, CRM association, modeled credit and causal evidence.

sources.title: [GA4] About data thresholds
sources.author: Google Analytics Help
sources.read_scope: Complete HTML response fetched (1,644,920 bytes); full article text read.
principles: Thresholding prevents inference about individual identities or sensitive information.
Demographic and search-query data may be withheld with insufficient counts.
Thresholds are system-defined; larger date ranges may change report availability.
limits: Specific platform privacy controls, not a complete privacy/legal compliance standard.
Broader windows change comparability and must be disclosed.
sources.applicability: Include threshold/coverage status, avoid re-identification, and do not treat withheld rows as zeros.

sources.title: Audio requirements
sources.principle: Audible, distortion-free and consistent spoken audio; encode for intended distribution and distinguish RSS from subscriber upload requirements.
sections: Best practices for audio on Apple Podcasts
sources.limits: Apple-specific recommendations, not universal recording specifications. Loudness guidance applies to delivery processing, not a source recording target. Does not supply recording backup procedure.
sources.coverage: Full extracted article read; no truncation.
sources.disposition: Background delivery guidance only; not cited as a recording standard.

sources.title: Captions and Transcripts
sources.principle: Synchronize captions; convey speech, speaker identity and meaningful sound; correct automatic text, names and timing; make accessible transcripts available with original content; preserve meaning.
sources.limits: Federal accessibility implementation guidance; not a legal compliance determination for Riggg. Numeric styling defaults are context-specific and not imported as universal scorecard thresholds. Captions alone do not establish full accessibility.
sources.coverage: Full extracted article read including examples and language/music/profanity guidance.

sources.title: Thumbnail & title tips
sources.principle: Represent the video accurately, front-load important title words, use readable uncomplicated thumbnails, consider intended audience and inspect channel-specific performance after publication.
sources.limits: Platform guidance, not experimental evidence that packaging causes business outcomes. Fetch hit 750000-byte HTML cap; substantive extracted guidance read but Types of video titles body missing and embedded video not watched. Do not use headline 90% statistic as causal proof.
sources.coverage: Entire available extracted article read; full-page completeness not certified. Retried 2026-10-08T21:10:00.542Z with same cap.
sources.disposition: Partial title-tips retrieval remains partial; omitted from public citations.

sources.title: Validate your podcast
sources.principle: Technical validation checks feed requirements, required tags and media/artwork availability; passing validation is not editorial approval. Diagnose actual access and enclosure errors.
sections: Common RSS feed validation error messages
sources.limits: Apple submission/feed validation, not proof a release reached its audience or succeeded; live URL and player checks are our operational extension.

sources.title: Section 3: Accuracy – Guidelines
sources.principle: Check factual claims and caveats; maintain research records for double-checking; edits must not materially mislead; archived/reused material may become outdated; correct substantive errors.
sources.limits: BBC editorial policy for its own output, not a Riggg mandate or marketing efficacy study; BBC referral machinery does not transfer to small teams.
sources.coverage: Complete extracted guidelines read using initial output and overflow log, including final corrections and nations section. Companion principles page also read.

sources.title: Measure key moments for audience retention
sources.principle: Interpret retention at video and audience-segment level; compare similar-length videos; spikes may mean interest or confusion; dips can reflect skipping or exiting; data needs processing time.
sections: Understand key moments for audience retention
View audience retention by segment type
View detailed activity for audience retention
sources.limits: YouTube-only definitions and eligibility. Current page says 1–2 day processing and key-moment eligibility of 60 seconds/100 views; those are platform conditions, not success thresholds. HTML byte cap means full page cannot be certified. No causal sales inference.
sources.coverage: All available extracted article through Metrics to know read; underlying HTML incomplete after 750000 bytes. Retry 2026-10-08T21:10:01.057Z same outcome.
sources.resolution: Duplicate of M5; full measurement retrieval resolves operations partial-text limitation. Cite M5 in article.

sources.title: Creating digital materials
sources.organization: Digital Preservation Coalition, Digital Preservation Handbook
sources.principle: Plan continuity at creation: find, open, work with, understand and trust files; use descriptive consistent filenames/versions, supported formats, explicit QA responsibilities, metadata and master/derivative organization.
sections: Preserving digital surrogates: digital preservation considerations
sources.limits: DPC-authored handbook guidance synthesizes preservation practice; not an original controlled study. Surrogate digitization practices are not all directly applicable to born-digital sessions. No proof that an archive generates commercial ROI or AEO visibility.
sources.coverage: Full extracted chapter including references read after recovering overflow log. Linked resources not treated as separately read evidence.

sources.title: Recommended Formats Statement – Moving Image Works
sources.principle: Keep identifiable complete final production versions with native production characteristics, relevant audio tracks and descriptive metadata; distinguish higher-quality preservation material from viewing proxies.
sources.limits: Library acquisition/preservation preferences, not compulsory creator codecs. Do not require IMF/FFV1/ProRes conversion for every small team, or infer that transcoding restores lost quality. No causal evidence of reuse outcomes.
sources.coverage: Full extracted page read; no truncation.

coverage_limits: Eight primary documents from four organizations (AMEC, IAB Tech Lab, Google, Apple), not eight independent empirical studies.
No paid sources, private analytics, client data or live session performance audited.
Google initial extraction body caps resolved by full-response article extraction.
IAB PDF initial raw extraction unreadable; all 29 pages subsequently read via installed pypdf.
No universal performance thresholds, 30-day standard, optimal sample size or causal ROI established.
Operational production and preservation checks are Riggg editorial application, not independently validated by these sources.
Publication dates unknown unless explicitly noted; retrieval timestamps are actual tool/server timestamps.
Search provider failed; direct known official URLs used. Not a systematic literature review.
W3C canonical accessibility pages returned 403; guessed official mirrors returned 404. GSA guidance successfully read instead.
Two Google sources have underlying HTML byte-cap warnings; available substantive text read, not full-page completeness.
No private analytics, actual client files, paid material, experiments or causal ROI evidence.
No recording-specific primary field-recording checklist successfully acquired; capture acceptance is editorial operational mapping of audio quality and preservation guidance.
